code_label: QAE offers quadratic Monte Carlo speedup
text_span: Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) can achieve a quadratic speed-up for applications classically solved by Monte Carlo simulation.
rationale: States the central motivation and performance claim for the paper's target algorithm.

code_label: State preparation is a key bottleneck
text_span: A key requirement to realize this advantage is efficient state preparation.
rationale: Identifies the main practical requirement that can determine whether the quantum advantage is preserved.

code_label: Generic state preparation is exponentially costly
text_span: preparing arbitrary quantum states has exponential complexity with respect to the number of qubits, thus, is not applicable.
rationale: States a fundamental limitation of generic state preparation for the intended use case.

code_label: Existing efficient methods are restricted
text_span: Currently known efficient techniques require problems based on log-concave probability distributions, involve learning an unknown distribution from empirical data, or fully rely on quantum arithmetic.
rationale: Summarizes the constraints of prior efficient approaches that the paper seeks to improve upon.

code_label: Paper introduces state-preparation simplification and circuit optimization
text_span: we introduce an approach to simplify state preparation, together with a circuit optimization technique, both of which can help reduce the circuit complexity for QAE state preparation significantly.
rationale: Captures the paper's main methodological contribution.

code_label: Demonstrations on hardware and Heston simulation
text_span: We demonstrate the introduced techniques for a numerical integration example on real quantum hardware, as well as for option pricing under the Heston model
rationale: Describes the empirical demonstrations used to validate the methods.

code_label: QAE error scales better than Monte Carlo
text_span: The resulting error scales as O(1/M), where M denotes the number of (quantum) samples, i.e., applications of Q.
rationale: States the asymptotic estimation advantage of QAE over classical sampling.

code_label: Monte Carlo error scales as inverse square root
text_span: the error resulting from Monte Carlo simulation scales as O(1/√M) for M (classical) samples
rationale: Provides the classical baseline used for comparison throughout the paper.

code_label: MLAE chosen for demonstrations
text_span: In the remainder of this paper we will consider MLAE for demonstrations, although our results are applicable to every variant of QAE.
rationale: Specifies the chosen QAE variant for experiments while noting broader applicability.

code_label: MLAE is practical but not guaranteed
text_span: MLAE does not provide a theoretical guarantee on the result, however, it performs well in practice and is well suited as benchmark
rationale: States a caveat about the selected estimation method.

code_label: Uniform distribution is easy to prepare
text_span: This is easy to prepare by applying Hadamard gates to all n state qubits.
rationale: Explains the simplest state-preparation case used as a building block.

code_label: Uniform loading becomes a Riemann sum
text_span: This can be interpreted as a left Riemann sum [18], i.e., a 2n-point approximation of the integral
rationale: Connects the quantum state preparation to numerical integration.

code_label: PDF times objective can estimate expectations
text_span: we can replace g in (5) by the product of f and g, which allows us to approximate the expectation value Ef[g(X)].
rationale: Describes the first extension from uniform loading to weighted expectations.

code_label: Multiplication avoids explicit quantum arithmetic
text_span: we do not have to explicitly multiply f and g using quantum arithmetic.
rationale: Highlights the simplification achieved by encoding multiplication in amplitudes.

code_label: Addition of functions via shared ancilla and Hadamard
text_span: we can also construct operators to realize addition of functions.
rationale: Introduces the second core amplitude-level operation.

code_label: Addition introduces a factor of one half
text_span: The addition introduces a factor of 1/2 that we need to take into account by multiplying the resulting estimate by a factor of 2.
rationale: States the normalization cost of the addition construction.

code_label: Error grows with repeated additions
text_span: This also increases the estimation error accordingly, which means that the error increases exponentially with the number of additions
rationale: Identifies a scaling caveat for repeated function addition.

code_label: Arbitrary combinations of additions and multiplications are possible
text_span: we can construct arbitrary combinations of additions and multiplications of functions
rationale: Summarizes the composability of the proposed amplitude-level operations.

code_label: Multivariate extension scales linearly in dimension
text_span: The required number of qubits will scale linearly in the dimension, unlike classical numerical integration schemes where the dependence is usually exponential
rationale: States the claimed scaling advantage for higher-dimensional problems.

code_label: Stochastic processes can be loaded through transition probabilities
text_span: we can load stochastic processes.
rationale: Introduces the extension from static distributions to stochastic processes.

code_label: Generic process loading via U is inefficient
text_span: like U in (2), cannot be done efficiently for generic processes.
rationale: States why the alternative loading approach is needed for stochastic processes.

code_label: Spin-echo can reduce circuit depth
text_span: we leverage an eﬀect that is also known as Spin-Echo [20]. In some cases, this can help to signiﬁcantly reduce the gates required
rationale: Introduces the circuit optimization technique and its intended benefit.

code_label: Rotation-reflection pattern simplifies to doubled rotation
text_span: RU(θ)V RU(−θ) = RU(2θ)V,
rationale: Gives the algebraic identity underlying the optimization.

code_label: QAE circuit can use half as many A applications
text_span: QkA can be constructed using only k+1 instead of 2k+1 applications of A
rationale: States the main circuit-depth reduction achieved by the optimization.

code_label: Optimization is compatible with amplitude addition and multiplication
text_span: This circuit optimization is compatible with the addition and multiplication techniques introduced in Sec. III.
rationale: Notes that the optimization can be combined with the earlier state-preparation constructions.

code_label: Discretization error must be added to QAE error
text_span: The discretization error needs to be added on top of the QAE estimation error, since QAE does not estimate the exact value but only an approximation.
rationale: States an important source of total error in the overall method.

code_label: Midpoint rule improves convergence without extra qubits
text_span: This leads to a better scaling, since the estimation error Emid_n is bounded by
rationale: Introduces the higher-order quadrature improvement.

code_label: Simpson's rule further improves scaling
text_span: Simpson’s rule leads to an even better scaling, since the estimation error ESimpson_n is bounded by
rationale: States the stronger convergence claim for the combined quadrature scheme.

code_label: Higher-order quadrature can be used without more qubits
text_span: Other quadrature rules for numerical integration, e.g., Romberg’s method / Richardson extrapolation, are also possible and lead to even higher orders of convergence, while keeping the number of grid points and qubits constant.
rationale: Indicates additional possible extensions beyond the demonstrated rules.

code_label: Non-equidistant grids are possible but more complex
text_span: Our approach can also be extended to non-equidistant grids, which allows the use of more advanced quadrature schemes
rationale: Describes a possible extension and its intended benefit.

code_label: Non-equidistant grids require quantum arithmetic
text_span: non-equidistant grids require computing the grid points using quantum arithmetic before evaluating the function g, leading to longer circuits
rationale: States the cost and complication of the non-equidistant-grid extension.

code_label: Multivariate midpoint error bound is additive over dimensions
text_span: The resulting error for the Midpoint rule Emid_n,d is bounded by
rationale: Introduces the multivariate error analysis.

code_label: High-dimensional schemes remain efficient for left, right, midpoint
text_span: For all three rules, we can achieve an exponential number of grid-points compared to the number of discretization qubits.
rationale: States the favorable scaling claim for multidimensional integration.

code_label: Other higher-order schemes scale less favorably in higher dimensions
text_span: Extending the other approaches to higher dimensions does not scale as favorably
rationale: Notes a limitation of extending more advanced quadrature rules to higher dimensions.

code_label: Hardware experiment uses sin-squared integral
text_span: Suppose the integral Z y x=0 sin2(πx)dx = 2πy − sin(2πy) 4π ,
rationale: Defines the numerical integration benchmark used in the hardware demonstration.

code_label: Hardware experiment uses one and two discretization qubits
text_span: we will use one and two qubits for the discretization, i.e., two and four discretization points, and an additional qubit to represent the function g.
rationale: Specifies the experimental discretization setup.

rationale: Describes the circuit construction used in the hardware experiment.

code_label: Readout and gate-noise mitigation applied
text_span: We apply readout error mitigation as well as error mitigation by inserting noisy gates combined with Richardson extrapolation
rationale: States the mitigation techniques used to improve hardware results.

code_label: Results show error decreases with more qubits and higher-order rules
text_span: It can be nicely observed how the approximation error reduces with increasing order of the applied quadrature rule, as well as with the increasing number of discretization points, i.e., qubits.
rationale: Summarizes the main empirical trend from the hardware experiment.

code_label: There is a threshold where model error dominates
text_span: For each quadrature rule there is a threshold, where the model error dominates the QAE estimation error
rationale: Identifies the point beyond which increasing QAE depth no longer helps.

code_label: MLAE can be numerically unstable
text_span: the lack of numerical robustness of MLAE, i.e., sometimes a small errors in the measured data can lead to a large deviation of the maximum likelihood estimate.
rationale: States a practical weakness observed in the estimation procedure.

code_label: Spin-echo reduces CNOT counts
text_span: the introduced circuit optimization technique can signiﬁcantly reduce the number of CNOT gates.
rationale: Summarizes the circuit-level benefit of the optimization.

code_label: Three-qubit circuits are more noise-sensitive than two-qubit circuits
text_span: the three qubit circuit can tolerate more noise before it starts to dominate the estimated values.
rationale: Explains the observed tradeoff between circuit size and noise tolerance.

code_label: Two-qubit circuit can be compressed to three CNOTs but does not scale
text_span: This can be achieved by ﬁrst classically evaluating the corresponding unitary matrix and then decomposing it into quantum gates again
rationale: Describes a special-case optimization and its scalability caveat.

code_label: Heston model used as illustrative stochastic-volatility example
text_span: The Heston model is an example of a stochastic volatility model used in financial mathematics to describe, for instance, the behavior of stock prices
rationale: Introduces the second application domain and model.

code_label: Heston dynamics discretized into transition laws
text_span: This allows us to derive the discrete transition laws as

code_label: Discounting is omitted for simplicity
text_span: For a constant interest rate, discounting just results in a simple correction term to compute the present value of the future payoﬀ.
rationale: States a simplification made in the option-pricing example.

code_label: Four qubits discretize volatility and stock paths
text_span: Thus, we use four qubits in total to discretize the volatility and stock price processes.
rationale: Specifies the qubit budget for the Heston-model demonstration.

code_label: Probability of all ancillas encodes normalized payoff
text_span: the probability of measuring |1111⟩ in the last four qubits, which equals 0.1185.
rationale: Reports the simulated output of the constructed circuit for the option-pricing example.

code_label: Method extends to exotic options and arbitrary stochastic processes
text_span: it is straightforward to extend the results in this paper to more exotic options, e.g., path-dependent options
rationale: Indicates broader applicability beyond the demonstrated European call option.

code_label: Future compilers may combine loading approaches automatically
text_span: it will result in a combination of different approaches automatically constructed by future quantum compilers.
rationale: States a forward-looking expectation about compiler support for state loading.
